info.title: SP Trading API
info.description:
Machine interface of SP Wallet: market data, portfolio, positions, orders, strategies and agents.

Authentication: `Authorization: Bearer spw_live_…` (an API key created by the owner with his passkey). A key opens nothing outside `/api/v1/trading/`.

Every operation names the scope it needs (`x-spw-scope`). Scopes are access control inside the API; they are not what bounds execution: an order placed with a key is bounded by a trading mandate that the isolated signer enforces, and execution scopes are inert without one.

Numbers that carry money are decimal strings. Paper and live data always carry a `mode` and are never merged.

Errors are `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<sentence>" }`, with `data` when a refusal has machine-readable detail (the order it is about, the mandate's reasons, the failed risk checks, the questions of an ambiguous command). Every operation lists the codes it can answer, with their status, in `x-spw-errors`. Rate limits are per key: `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds).

A path that is not an operation of this document (or a known path with another method) answers 404 `not_found` in the same error model.

An order's `status` is one of the twelve states of `x-spw-order-states`; `final` is true for the states marked final. `UNKNOWN` is neither final nor a failure. Lists that can grow without bound (`GET /orders`, `GET /activity`) are paginated with `cursor` / `nextCursor`.

get.summary: Instruments across venues (perpetuals) and the spot market-data symbols
get.description: Each row carries the time its source produced it (`ts`) and a `stale` flag. A venue that cannot be read is listed in `errors`; when no source answers the call fails with 503. get.summary: Compare the estimated cost of one position across venues
get.description: One row per venue for a common underlying, from the real instrument, order book (GMX: pool figures), ticker, fee schedule and funding rate read now: spread, depth within 10/25/50 bps, slippage for the notional, fees, funding expected over the horizon (current rate held constant), collateral, liquidation estimate and the itemised total. Every figure is an estimate; a missing input gives null with its reason. Venues the wallet cannot trade on are shown and flagged. `discrepancies` are estimates with their assumptions and risks, never a recommendation.

post.description: Idempotent on (principal, Idempotency-Key): a replay answers the same order and never sends a second request to a venue; the same key with a different order answers 409 `idempotency_conflict`. Owner session: the order is checked and waits `AWAITING_APPROVAL` until the owner approves it with the passkey in the app (paper: executed at once, nothing is signed). API key: needs a trading mandate bound to the key that covers the order exactly (403 `mandate_denied` with the reasons otherwise), then the risk engine, then the venue engine's mandate path — the isolated signer applies the derivative mandate it stores. LIVE needs `SPW_TRADING_API_EXECUTION=on` on the server (403 `execution_disabled` otherwise) and the existing mainnet locks. A refusal after the order exists answers 4xx with the order in `data.order` (state `REJECTED` or `FAILED`). An outcome that is not known is `UNKNOWN`, never a failure. Spot orders: 403 `spot_execution_requires_agent_vault` for a key; 422 `spot_via_swap_screen` for the owner. The venue engine that executes the order can refuse it with a code of its own rules that this list does not name (`x-spw-errors-open`): the HTTP status still tells the class, and the order is in `data.order`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replay protection: 8 to 100 characters (letters, digits, . _ : -). The same key with the same request returns the first answer; with a different request, 409 `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: X-SPW-Timestamp
parameters.description: Optional freshness check: Unix seconds; refused (400 `stale_request`) when more than 300 s from the server clock.

The answer carries the size that was used. Exactly one of `size` and `notional` is required

At the venue the order is `CANCELLED` when the venue says so. An order that is already final answers 200 with `changed: false`.

post.summary: Preview an order: every check it would meet, and an estimate
post.description: Resolves the instrument and the account, then runs the key limits, the server locks, the trading mandate (keys and agents), the independent risk engine and the venue engine's own checks on the market as it is now. Answers the canonical order and its hash, every check with what was observed and its limit, an estimate (fees, slippage against the real book, liquidation price) and whether an owner passkey approval would be required. Never creates, signs or sends anything; takes no Idempotency-Key. What WOULD refuse the order is in `refusals` (HTTP 200), not an error answer. Account figures (equity, free collateral, positions) are answered only to a key that also holds `wallet:read` or `positions:read` (`account.withheld`).

post.summary: Run one line of the trading command grammar
post.description: Deterministic grammar (no model). The scope checked is the one of the operation the command resolves to: an order needs `orders:execute` (`orders:prepare` with `dryRun`), CLOSE `positions:manage`, CANCEL `orders:cancel`, SHOW the matching read scope, KILL `positions:manage`. Resolution uses the owner's stored defaults (GET/PUT /api/v1/developer/command-defaults) and nothing else: a command the defaults do not settle answers 409 `ambiguous_command` with the questions in `data.questions` and executes nothing. `kind` says what the command resolved to: `query` (the read answer is in `data`), `control` (a cancel or the kill switch) or `order`. STOP ALL AGENTS answers 501 `execution_not_wired`. The venue engine that executes the order can refuse it with a code of its own rules that this list does not name (`x-spw-errors-open`): the HTTP status still tells the class, and the order is in `data.order`.
